cues.en: Mike, welcome.
cues.zh: Mike，欢迎你。

cues.en: It's good to see you.
cues.zh: 很高兴见到你。

cues.en: I'm excited for this conversation.
cues.zh: 我很期待这次对话。

cues.en: Thank you so much. I'm so happy to be here.
cues.zh: 非常感谢，我也很高兴能来这里。

cues.en: So most of us have this mental model in biology
cues.zh: 我们在生物学上大多有这样一个认知模型，

cues.en: that DNA is the property of every living thing,
cues.zh: 认为 DNA 是所有生物的共有属性，

cues.en: that it is kind of the software that builds the hardware of our body.
cues.zh: 它有点像构建我们身体硬件的软件。

cues.en: That's how a lot of us think about this.
cues.zh: 我们很多人都是这么想的。

cues.en: That model leaves too many deep mysteries.
cues.zh: 但这个模型留下了太多未解的深层谜团。

cues.en: Can you share with us some of those mysteries?
cues.zh: 你能跟我们分享其中一些谜团吗？

cues.en: and also what tadpoles have to do with it?
cues.zh: 还有，这跟蝌蚪又有什么关系？

cues.en: Sure. Yeah, I'd like to give you another perspective on this problem.
cues.zh: 当然可以。我想从另一个角度来看待这个问题。

cues.en: So one of the things that DNA does is specify the hardware of each cell.
cues.zh: DNA 所做的事情之一，就是指定每个细胞的硬件结构。

cues.en: So the DNA tells every cell what proteins it's supposed to have.
cues.zh: DNA 会告诉每个细胞它应该具备哪些蛋白质。

cues.en: And so when you have tadpoles, for example,
cues.zh: 比如在观察蝌蚪时，

cues.en: you see the kind of thing that most people think is sort of a progressive unrolling
cues.zh: 大多数人认为看到的，是某种基因组特定基因开启和关闭的

cues.en: of the genome-specific genes turned on and off,
cues.zh: 渐进式展开过程，

cues.en: and a tadpole as it becomes a frog has to rearrange its face. So the eyes, the
cues.zh: 蝌蚪长成青蛙时必须重塑它的面部。所以眼睛、

cues.en: nostrils, the jaws, everything has to move. And one way to think about it used
cues.zh: 鼻孔、下颌，所有部位都必须移动。过去人们的一种

cues.en: to be that, well, you have a sort of hardwired set of movements where all of
cues.zh: 看法是，存在一组固定的运动模式，

cues.en: these things move around and then you get your frog. Actually, a few years ago
cues.zh: 所有这些器官各自移动到位，就变成了青蛙。实际上几年前，

cues.en: we found a pretty amazing phenomenon, which is that if you make so-called
cues.zh: 我们发现了一个非常惊人的现象，那就是如果你制造出所谓的

cues.en: Picasso Frogs, so these are tadpoles where the jaws might be off to the
cues.zh: “毕加索青蛙”，也就是那些下颌可能会偏向一侧的蝌蚪，

cues.en: side, the eyes are up here, you know, the nostrils are moved, so everything is
cues.zh: 侧面，眼睛在这上面，鼻孔也移位了，所以一切都

cues.en: shifted. These tapels make largely normal frog faces. Now this is amazing because all of the
cues.zh: 变位了。这些蝌蚪却大多长出了正常的蛙脸。这很不可思议，因为所有

cues.en: organs start off in abnormal positions and yet they still end up making a pretty good frog face.
cues.zh: 器官初始位置都不对，但最终还是形成了一张相当不错的蛙脸。

cues.en: And so what it turns out is that this system, like many living systems, is not a hardwired
cues.zh: 事实证明，这个系统就像许多生命系统一样，并非一套写死的

cues.en: set of movements but actually works to reduce the error between what's going on now and what it
cues.zh: 固定动作，而是实际在努力缩小现状与它所

cues.en: knows is a correct frog face configuration. This kind of decision making that involves flexible
cues.zh: 认知的正常蛙脸结构之间的误差。这种决策过程涉及对新情况的

cues.en: responses to new circumstances. In other contexts we would call this intelligence.
cues.zh: 灵活应对。在其他语境下，我们会称之为智能。

cues.en: And so what we need to understand now is not only the mechanisms by which these
cues.zh: 所以我们现在需要理解的，不仅是这些细胞

cues.en: cells execute their movements and gene expression and so on, but we really have
cues.zh: 执行移动和基因表达等过程的机制，更必须

cues.en: to understand the information flow. How do these cells cooperate with each other
cues.zh: 理解其中的信息流。这些细胞是如何协同合作

cues.en: to build something large and to stop building when that specific structure
cues.zh: 构建出大型结构，并在特定结构建成后

cues.en: is created? And these kinds of computations, not just the mechanisms,
cues.zh: 停止构建的？而这类计算过程，不仅仅是底层机制，

cues.en: but the computations are of anatomical control for the future of biology.
cues.zh: 更是生物学未来在解剖结构控制层面的核心计算。

cues.en: And so I guess the traditional model is that somehow cells are sending
cues.zh: 我想传统的模型大概是认为，细胞在以某种方式相互发送

cues.en: biochemical signals to each other that allow development to happen in the smart way.
cues.zh: 生物化学信号，让发育能够如此巧妙地进行。

cues.en: But do you think there is something else at work? What is that?
cues.zh: 但你觉得还有其他机制在起作用吗？那是什么？

cues.en: Well, cells certainly do communicate biochemically and via physical forces,
cues.zh: 嗯，细胞确实会通过生物化学和物理力来进行交流，

cues.en: but there's something else that's going on that's extremely interesting.
cues.zh: 但还有另一种机制在起作用，而且非常有趣。

cues.en: And that is that it's basically called bioelectricity,
cues.zh: 那基本上就是所谓的生物电，

cues.en: non-neural bioelectricity.
cues.zh: 非神经元生物电。

cues.en: So it turns out that all cells, not just nerves,
cues.zh: 事实证明，所有的细胞，不仅仅是神经细胞，

cues.en: but all cells in your body communicate
cues.zh: 身体里的所有细胞都会

cues.en: with each other using electrical signals.
cues.zh: 利用电信号相互交流。

cues.en: And what you're seeing here is a time lapse video
cues.zh: 你们在这里看到的是一段延时摄影视频，

cues.en: for the first time, we are now able to eavesdrop
cues.zh: 我们现在首次能够偷听

cues.en: on all of the electrical conversations
cues.zh: 细胞之间进行的

cues.en: that the cells are having with each other.
cues.zh: 所有电信号对话。

cues.en: So think about this, we're now watching,
cues.zh: 想想看，我们现在看到的，

cues.en: this is an early frog embryo,
cues.zh: 是一个早期的青蛙胚胎，

cues.en: this is about eight hours to 10 hours of development,
cues.zh: 发育时间大概在八到十个小时，

cues.en: and the colors are showing you actual electrical states
cues.zh: 这些颜色展示的是真实的电状态，

cues.en: that allows you to see all of the electrical software
cues.zh: 让你能看到所有的电信号“软件”，

cues.en: that's running on the genome-defined cellular hardware.
cues.zh: 正运行在基因组决定的细胞“硬件”之上。

cues.en: And so these cells are basically communicating
cues.zh: 所以这些细胞基本是在互相沟通，

cues.en: with each other who's going to be head,
cues.zh: 谁来发育成头，

cues.en: who's going to be tail, who's going to be left and right
cues.zh: 谁发育成尾巴，谁在左谁在右，

cues.en: and make eyes and brain and so on.
cues.zh: 以及长出眼睛和大肠等等。

cues.en: And so it is this software that allows these living systems
cues.zh: 正是这种“软件”，让这些生命系统

cues.en: to achieve specific goals,
cues.zh: 能够实现特定的目标，

cues.en: goals such as building an embryo
cues.zh: 比如构建出一个胚胎，

cues.en: or regenerating a limb for animals that do this.
cues.zh: 或者对于某些动物来说，再生肢体。

cues.en: And the ability to see these electrical conversations
cues.zh: 而能够看到这些电信号的对话，

cues.en: gives us some really remarkable opportunities
cues.zh: 给我们带来了极其难得的机遇，

cues.en: to target or to rewrite the goals
cues.zh: 去定向干预甚至改写

cues.en: towards which these living systems are operating.
cues.zh: 这些生命系统运作所朝向的目标。

cues.en: OK, so this is pretty radical.
cues.zh: 好，这想法相当颠覆。

cues.en: Let me see if I understand this.
cues.zh: 我看看我理解得对不对。

cues.en: What you're saying is that when an organism starts to develop,
cues.zh: 你是说，当一个生物体开始发育时，

cues.en: as soon as a cell divides, electrical signals are shared between them
cues.zh: 细胞一旦分裂，彼此间就会共享电信号，

cues.en: but as you get to, what, a few hundred cells,
cues.zh: 但当细胞数量达到，比方说几百个时，

cues.en: that somehow these signals end up forming a kind of,
cues.zh: 这些信号不知怎么的，最终形成了一种，

cues.en: essentially like a computer program,
cues.zh: 本质上就像计算机程序一样的东西，

cues.en: a program that somehow includes all the information needed
cues.zh: 这个程序不知怎么就包含了所有所需的信息，

cues.en: to tell that organism what its destiny is.
cues.zh: 来告诉那个生物体它未来的命运。

cues.en: Is that the right way to think about it?
cues.zh: 这么理解对吗？

cues.en: Yes, quite.
cues.zh: 是的，完全没错。

cues.en: Basically what happens is that these cells,
cues.zh: 基本上发生的事情是，这些细胞

cues.en: by forming electrical networks, much like networks in the brain,
cues.zh: 通过形成电网络——很像大脑中的网络，

cues.en: They form electrical networks, and these networks process information, including pattern memories.
cues.zh: 它们形成电网络，而这些网络会处理信息，包括模式记忆。

cues.en: representation of large-scale anatomical structures
cues.zh: 宏观解剖结构的表征，

cues.en: where various organs will go,
cues.zh: 各个器官将长在何处，

cues.en: what the different axes of the animal,
cues.zh: 动物的不同轴向，

cues.en: front and back, head and tail, are going to be,
cues.zh: 前后、头尾，会是什么样，

cues.en: and these are literally held in the electrical circuits
cues.zh: 而这些信息就切实地保存在大片组织的电路中，

cues.en: across large tissues in the same way
cues.zh: 其机制与大脑保存

cues.en: that brains hold other kinds of memories and learning.
cues.zh: 其他记忆和学习成果的方式如出一辙。

cues.en: So is this the right way to think about it?
cues.zh: 所以这么理解对吗？

cues.en: Because this seems to me such a big shift.
cues.zh: 因为在我看来，这是一个巨大的转变。

cues.en: I mean, when I first got a computer,
cues.zh: 我是说，当我第一次接触电脑时，

cues.en: I was in awe of the people who could kind of do so-called machine code,
cues.zh: 我非常敬佩那些能写所谓机器码的人，

cues.en: like the direct programming of individual bits in the computer.
cues.zh: 也就是直接对计算机里的每一个比特进行编程。

cues.en: That was impossible for most mortals.
cues.zh: 对绝大多数凡人来说，这根本不可能做到。

cues.en: To have a chance of controlling that computer,
cues.zh: 想要掌控那台电脑，

cues.en: you'd have to program in a language,
cues.zh: 你就必须用一种编程语言来写代码，

cues.en: which was just a vastly simpler way of making big picture things happen.
cues.zh: 这是一种能从宏观层面实现功能的简单得多的方式。

cues.en: And if I understand you right, what you're saying is that most of biology today
cues.zh: 如果我没理解错的话，你的意思是如今的大多数生物学研究，

cues.en: has sort of taken place trying to do the equivalent of machine code programming,
cues.zh: 在某种程度上都相当于在做机器码层面的编程，

cues.en: of understanding the biochemical signals between individual cells,
cues.zh: 试图去理解单个细胞之间的生化信号，

cues.en: when, wait a sec, holy crap, there's this language going on,
cues.zh: 然而，等等，我的天啊，其实一直存在这样一种语言，

cues.en: this electrical language,
cues.zh: 一种电信号语言，

cues.en: which, if you could understand that,
cues.zh: 如果我们能够理解它，

cues.en: that would give us a completely different set of insights
cues.zh: 就会为我们带来一套截然不同的全新视角，

cues.en: into how organisms are developed.
cues.zh: 去认识生物体究竟是如何发育的。

cues.en: Is that metaphor basically right?
cues.zh: 这个比喻基本恰当吗？

cues.en: Yeah, this is exactly right.
cues.zh: 对，完全没错。

cues.en: So if you think about the way programming was done in the 40s,
cues.zh: 想想看 40 年代人们是怎么编程的，

cues.en: in order to get your computer to do something different,
cues.zh: 为了让计算机执行不同的任务，

cues.en: that you would physically have to shift the wires around.
cues.zh: 你必须亲自动手重新接线。

cues.en: So you would have to go in there and rewire the hardware.
cues.zh: 也就是说，你得钻进去对硬件重新布线。

cues.en: You would have to interact with the hardware directly,
cues.zh: 你必须直接和硬件打交道，

cues.en: and all of your strategies for manipulating that machine
cues.zh: 所有操控那台机器的策略，

cues.en: would be at the level of the hardware.
cues.zh: 都停留在硬件层面。

cues.en: And the reason we have this now amazing technology
cues.zh: 而我们如今之所以能迎来这场惊人的科技革命、

cues.en: revolution, information sciences, and so on,
cues.zh: 信息科学等等，

cues.en: is because computer science moved from a focus
cues.zh: 正是因为计算机科学的重心

cues.en: on the hardware onto understanding
cues.zh: 从硬件转移开来，并认识到

cues.en: that if your hardware is good enough,
cues.zh: 只要你的硬件足够好——

cues.en: and I'm going to tell you that biological hardware
cues.zh: 而我想告诉你的是，生物硬件

cues.en: is absolutely good enough,
cues.zh: 绝对足够好——

cues.en: then you can interact with your system not by
cues.zh: 那么你就可以与系统交互，而不需要

cues.en: tweaking or rewiring the hardware but actually you can take a step back
cues.zh: 去调整或重接硬件，实际上你可以退后一步，

cues.en: and give it stimuli or inputs the way that you would give to a reprogrammable
cues.zh: 像给可重编程计算机输入数据那样

cues.en: computer
cues.zh: 给它刺激或输入，

cues.en: and cause the cellular network to do something completely
cues.zh: 从而促使细胞网络做出

cues.en: different than it would otherwise have done.
cues.zh: 与以往截然不同的反应。

cues.en: So this, the ability to see these bioelectrical signals
cues.zh: 所以，能够观测到这些生物电信号的能力

cues.en: is giving us an entry point directly into the software that guides large-scale
cues.zh: 为我们提供了一个切入点，让我们能直接接触到引导宏观

cues.en: anatomy
cues.zh: 解剖结构的底层软件

cues.en: which is a very different approach to medicine
cues.zh: 这与重新改造每个细胞内部的特定通路相比，

cues.en: than to rewiring specific pathways inside of every cell.
cues.zh: 是一种截然不同的医学思路。

cues.en: And so in many ways, the amazingness of your work
cues.zh: 所以在很多层面上，你这项工作的惊人之处在于

cues.en: is that you're starting to crack the code
cues.zh: 你开始破译

cues.en: of these electrical signals,
cues.zh: 这些电信号的密码了，

cues.en: and you've got an amazing demonstration of this
cues.zh: 而且你在这些扁虫身上

cues.en: in these flatworms.
cues.zh: 做出了令人惊叹的验证演示。

cues.en: Tell us what's going on here.
cues.zh: 快给我们讲讲这里面的奥秘吧。

cues.en: So this is a creature known as a planarian.
cues.zh: 这种生物叫做涡虫。

cues.en: They're flatworms.
cues.zh: 它们属于扁虫。

cues.en: They're actually quite a complex creature.
cues.zh: 其实它们是相当复杂的生物。

cues.en: They have a true brain,
cues.zh: 它们拥有真正意义上的大脑、

cues.en: lots of different organs, and so on.
cues.zh: 许多不同的器官，等等。

cues.en: And the amazing thing about these planaria is that they are highly, highly regenerative.
cues.zh: 而且这些涡虫最神奇的地方在于，它们具有极强、极强的再生能力。

cues.en: So if you cut it into pieces, in fact, over 200 pieces, every piece will rebuild exactly
cues.zh: 如果你把它切成碎片，实际上即使切成200多块，每一块都会精确地重新构建

cues.en: what's needed to make a perfect little worm.
cues.zh: 长成一条完美小涡虫所需的全部结构。

cues.en: So think about that.
cues.zh: 想想看这意味着什么。

cues.en: This is a system where every single piece knows exactly what a correct planaria looks
cues.zh: 在这个系统里，每一个碎片都确切知道一只正常的涡虫应该长成什么样，

cues.en: like and builds the right organs in the right places and then stops.
cues.zh: 并且会在正确的位置长出正确的器官，然后停止生长。

cues.en: And that's one of the most amazing things about regeneration.
cues.zh: 这也是再生最神奇的地方之一。

cues.en: So what we discovered is that if you cut it into three pieces and amputate the head and
cues.zh: 我们的发现是，如果你把它切成三段，切掉头部和

cues.en: the tail, and you just take this middle fragment, which is what you see here, amazingly, there
cues.zh: 尾部，只留下中间这一截（也就是你们在这里看到的），神奇的是，它会产生一个

cues.en: is an electrical gradient, head to tail that's generated, that tells the piece where the
cues.zh: 从头到尾的电位梯度，告诉这个组织块

cues.en: heads and the tails go, and in fact, how many heads or tails you're supposed to have.
cues.zh: 头部和尾部该长在哪里，实际上，甚至能决定该长出几个头或几条尾巴。

cues.en: So what we learned to do is to manipulate this electrical gradient, and the important
cues.zh: 所以我们学会了去操控这种电位梯度，而重点

cues.en: thing is that we don't apply electricity.
cues.zh: 在于我们并没有施加外加电。

cues.en: What we do instead was we turn on and off the little transistors. They're
cues.zh: 我们做的是去开关那些微型晶体管。它们

cues.en: actually ion channel proteins that every cell natively uses to set up this
cues.zh: 其实是每个细胞自身用来建立这种电状态的

cues.en: electrical state and so now we have ways to turn them on and off and when you do
cues.zh: 离子通道蛋白，如今我们有了开关它们的方法，而当你这样做时，

cues.en: this one of the things you can do is you can shift that circuit to a state that
cues.zh: 其中一件能做到的事，就是你可以将那个回路切换到一种状态，

cues.en: says no build two heads or in fact build no heads and what you're seeing
cues.zh: 发出指令：“长出两个头”，或者其实也可以是“一个头都不长”，而你们在这里

cues.en: here are real worms that have either two or no heads that result from this
cues.zh: 看到的就是由此产生的真正长了两个头或没有头的虫子，

cues.en: because that electrical map is what the cells are using to decide what to do.
cues.zh: 因为细胞正是利用这种电信号图谱来决定该做什么的。

cues.en: And so what you're seeing here are live two-headed worms,
cues.zh: 所以大家在这里看到的是活生生的双头虫，

cues.en: and having generated these, we did a completely crazy experiment.
cues.zh: 培育出它们之后，我们又做了一个极其疯狂的实验。

cues.en: You take one of these two-headed worms and you chop off both heads,
cues.zh: 如果你抓来这样一条双头扁虫，切掉它的两个头，

cues.en: and you leave just a normal middle fragment.
cues.zh: 只留下一段正常的中间身体。

cues.en: Now, keep in mind, these animals have not been genomically edited.
cues.zh: 记住，这些动物并没有经过基因编辑。

cues.en: There's absolutely nothing different about their genomes.
cues.zh: 它们的基因组绝对没有任何改变。

cues.en: Their genomic sequence is completely wild-type.
cues.zh: 它们的基因组序列完全是野生型的。

cues.en: So you amputate the heads, you've got a nice normal fragment, and then you ask in
